Content: Select `bbtext(three)` details from the passage that should be included in a summary.

A.Choice: “'There's no off-the-shelf . . . turtle bathing suit that we know about,' laughed biologist Ken Lohmann, as he attached a soft cloth harness, or bathing suit, to a three-month-old loggerhead turtle.” (paragraph 1)

B.Choice: “But the hatchlings seem to be programmed with an astonishing 'Survival To Do List.'” (paragraph 3)

C.Choice: “'We've found over the years that one of the turtles' main tricks for navigation is that they are exquisitely sensitive to the Earth's magnetic field,' said Lohmann.” (paragraph 6)

D.Choice: “For example, there's a magnetic field off Portugal that triggers the turtles to turn south.” (paragraph 8)

E.Choice: “'The turtles will actually act out their swimming behavior in air,' said Lohmann.” (paragraph 17)

F.Choice: “The dramatic connection between turtles and magnetic fields is already altering conservation efforts for these reptiles.” (paragraph 23)

G.Choice: “'The people who are involved in our research usually are passionate about both science and conservation.'” (paragraph 27)

Topics: Reading Information - Central Ideas & Themes Of Texts
SubTopics: Determine one or more central ideas of an informational text and analyze how it is developed and refined over the course of a text, including how it emerges and is shaped by specific details; provide an objective summary of the text.
Content: This question has `bbtext(two)` parts. First, answer Part A. Then, answer Part B.
What is a central idea of the passage?

A.Choice: Sea turtles change their migration patterns as they age.

B.Choice: Sea turtles can be rehabilitated using newly discovered methods.

C.Choice: Sea turtles use magnetic fields to navigate along their migration routes.

D.Choice: Sea turtles are taught to swim at an early age in order to escape predators.

Content: Which sentence from the passage develops the central idea in Part A?

A.Choice: “'Their entire survival strategy seems to be predicated on the idea that the faster you get away from land, the better,' he said.” (paragraph 4)

B.Choice: “'In effect, sea turtles have a crude global positioning system that is based on the Earth's magnetic field,' said Lohmann.” (paragraph 14)

C.Choice: “Older turtles might spend an hour to an hour and a half swimming (or 'air swimming') for this navigation research.” (paragraph 19)

D.Choice: “Lohmann's study of animals and magnetism began when he was studying neurobiology, working with sea slugs as a graduate student.” (paragraph 22)

Topics: Reading Literature - Interactions Among Text Elements
SubTopics: Analyze how an author unfolds and develops ideas throughout a text, including how complex characters (e.g., those with multiple or conflicting motivations) develop, interact with other characters, and advance the plot or develop the theme.
Content: This question has `bbtext(two)` parts. First, answer Part A. Then, answer Part B.
In “Narcissus Myth,” how is the reader's understanding of Echo different from Narcissus's understanding of Echo?

A.Choice: The reader does not know that Echo admires the beauty of Narcissus, but Narcissus knows this.

B.Choice: The reader knows the feelings that Echo wants to express, but Narcissus does not know this.

C.Choice: The reader does not know Echo has a limited power to speak, but Narcissus knows this.

D.Choice: The reader knows that Echo is a nymph, but Narcissus does not know this.

Content: How does the difference described in Part A affect the tone of the passage?

A.Choice: It creates a humorous tone because of Narcissus's love of himself.

B.Choice: It creates an inspiring tone because of Echo's determination to speak.

C.Choice: It creates an angry tone because of Narcissus's negative attitude toward others.

D.Choice: It creates a hopeless tone because of Echo's inability to speak in her own words.

Content: Select `bbtext(before)` the sentence from paragraph 3 of “Narcissus Myth” that `bbtext(best)` explains what causes Narcissus to become obsessed with looking at himself.

:ibox:	 :MC-A: So Narcissus went on his cruel way, a scorner of love. :MC-B: But at last one of those he wounded prayed a prayer and it was answered by the gods: “May he who loves not others love himself.” :MC-C: The great goddess Nemesis, which means righteous anger, undertook to bring this about. :MC-D: As Narcissus bent over a clear pool for a drink and saw there his own reflection, on the moment he fell in love with it. :MC-E: “Now I know,” he cried, “what others have suffered from me, for I burn with love of my own self—and yet how can I reach that loveliness I see mirrored in the water? :MC-F: But I cannot leave it. G Only death can set me free.” :MC-H: And so it happened. :MC-I: He pined away, leaning perpetually over the pool, fixed in one long gaze. :MC-J: Echo was near him, but she could do nothing; only when, dying, he called to his image, “Farewell—farewell,” she could repeat the words as a last good-by to him. (paragraph 3)

Topics: Reading Literature - Perspective & Purpose In Texts
SubTopics: Determine an author's lens in a text (including cultural experience reflected in a work of literature from outside the United States, drawing on a wide reading of world literature) and analyze how an author uses rhetorical devices to advance a point of view.
Content: Which statement accurately explains why the Oreads are surprised by the pool's reaction to Narcissus's death in “The Disciple”?

A.Choice: The Oreads had thought that the pool did not know that Narcissus died, but the pool does know this.

B.Choice: The Oreads had thought that the pool was filled with Narcissus's tears, but the tears are not from Narcissus.

C.Choice: The Oreads had thought that the pool would need to be comforted because Narcissus died, but the pool does not know Narcissus.

D.Choice: The Oreads had thought that the pool was sad about losing Narcissus's beauty, but the pool is sad about losing the opportunity to view itself.
